text: In Plotinus's three-tiered ontology (the One, Intellect, Soul), which hypostasis has eternity (aion) as its mode of being — a life that is complete, all together, and without succession?
explanation: Intellect grasps all the Forms at once in a single undivided act, and this 'all together' (homou) completeness just is Plotinian eternity (aion). The One is beyond being and thought — temporal categories do not even apply to it, so it is not 'eternal' in the technical aion sense; Soul, by contrast, is discursive and sequential and is precisely the hypostasis that generates time; and the cosmos is temporal because it is animated by Soul.
